question: Which temple is known as 'black pagoda'?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Konark Sun Temple**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Konark Sun Temple**

 
 
• **​**It **Located in Odisha, India, the Konark Sun Temple is a 13th-century temple dedicated to the Hindu sun god, Surya.**
 
• Its massive **chariot-like structure,** with intricately carved wheels and horses, was designed to appear as though the sun god was riding through the sky.
 
• Due to its **dark colour and magnetic aura, sailors called it the "Black Pagoda," as it was visible from afar along the coast and sometimes caused compass deviations.**
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Sit**e and a significant example of Kalinga architecture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suryanar Temple**

 
 
• Situated in **Tamil Nadu, India, Suryanar Templ**e is a Hindu temple dedicated to Surya, the sun god.
 
• **Built in the 11th century by Chola King Kulothunga**, it is part of the Navagraha (nine planetary deities) temples.
 
• This temple uniquely features shrines for all nine planetary deities in Hindu astrology, with Surya as the central deity.
 
• It is **an important pilgrimage site for followers seeking astrological remedies.**
 
 
 
• **Martand Sun Templ**e
 
 
• Located in Kashmir, India, t**he Martand Sun Temple was built by King Lalitaditya Muktapida in the 8th century.**
 
• **This ancient temple is dedicated to the sun god, Surya, and showcases a unique blend of Gandharan, Gupta, and Kashmiri architectural styl**es.
 
• Although it is now mostly in ruins, it is considered one of the most impressive ancient Hindu temples in North India and reflects the region's rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Shani Shingnapu**r
 
 
• This temple,** located in Maharashtra, India, is dedicated to Shani, the god associated with the planet Saturn.**
 
• Unlike other temples, it does not have a traditional structure or idol but rather a simple black stone that symbolizes Shani.
 
• Shani Shingnapur is famous for its unique open-air shrine, and the village is notable for having houses without doors, as residents believe Shani protects them from theft and crime.
